text:
morgan: quick kickoff: i'm prototyping a rollout UX for automatic fallbacks that emphasizes observability + webhook integrations for downstream telemetry sinks. want to capture requirements before i mock screens.
arya: nice. what kinds of webhooks are we talking? incident hooks, billing, or customer-facing change events?
devin: all of the above. core idea: when a fallback fires, we emit a compact event to a configured webhook (if customer opted in) that includes only non-PII metadata: fallback_token, policy_id, reason, variant, timestamp, and normalized_cost_estimate. no prompt contents.
srinivas: +1 but customers will ask for examples. propose two webhook flavors: summary (one-line event) and sampled (includes a small redacted snippet if customer has sampling turned on). sampling governed by rollout-level sample_rate.
lex: UX note: in the rollout table show a "Webhooks" column. allow toggling summary vs sampled for each environment (prod/staging). also show recent delivery status and last-failed timestamp.
morgan: good. delivery guarantees: we send async POSTs and surface delivery status in console (success/failure, latency, 5xx code). provide a retry window (48h) and a retention TTL for sampled payloads (30d default).
devin: security: webhook payloads must be signed. include an HMAC header `X-Redwood-Signature` and docs on key rotation. also rate-limit webhook deliveries per-customer.
srinivas: billing implication: if fallback is a cheaper model, we still need to show both normalized and raw units in billing export. i want webhook summary to carry both fields so downstream pipelines can reconcile costs. field names: normalized_units, raw_units_breakdown (stringified).
arya: console UX: when viewing a rollout, add a small "fallback heatmap" that shows top reasons over time and top customers affected. clicking a bucket opens sampled examples (if sampling enabled). also allow filtering by webhook delivery status.
morgan: audit trail: every webhook trigger should also create an internal audit row linking fallback_token -> webhook_delivery_id -> decision_record_id so forensic queries can join them. retention default 30d; enterprise 365d.
lex: operators will want an endpoint to replay sampled events to a different webhook (for debugging). must be admin-only and create an explicit audit entry "replay by <user> at <ts>".
devin: API change: add response header `X-Redwood-Fallback-Token: fh_<policy>_<shortid>` when fallback occurs. webhook will include the token too. token resolution API: GET /internal/fallbacks/{token} -> returns decision metadata (gated).
srinivas: implementation note: token generation should be deterministic for identical decision tuples within a short window to avoid blowup during retries; but still include randomness so attackers can't enumerate. maybe HMAC over tuple with salt + short hex.
arya: QA: add a synthetic traffic toggle in the rollout UI that can replay a set of canned inputs to test fallback behavior and webhook flows. results feed into a small QA report (counts, webhook successes, avg latency).
morgan: privacy: never include prompt text in summary webhooks. sampled webhooks can include redacted_preview (first 80 chars) and prompt_hash. require explicit customer opt-in for full prompt in enterprise-only exports.
opsbot: deploybot: feature/fallback-webhooks enabled in staging at 4385001150 by ci-user :white_check_mark:
devin: last question: should webhook failures affect rollout decisions? e.g., if webhooks downstream are failing, do we stop sampling? my feeling: keep decision logic orthogonal; surface failure metrics so humans can act. automatic throttling for failed webhooks could be an optional safety toggle.
lex: agreed. add "adaptive sampling" opt-in that reduces sampled webhook rate if delivery error rate > 10% over 5m. console shows toggle and current status.
srinivas: i'll draft the token format, webhook payload schema (flat), and the internal resolution API spec. can we review in the 30m sync?
morgan: perfect — i'll add a tiny mockup for the rollout row and webhook modal and post it before the sync. thanks all!
